E., Miller, J., Orrell, T., Aalbu, R., Abbott, J., Aedo, C., Aescht, E., et al. (2026). Catalogue of Life (Version 2026-08-20). Catalogue of Life Foundation, Amsterdam, Netherlands. https://doi.org/10.48580/dgywk
scope: Only taxonRank=species and taxonomicStatus=accepted are counted as accepted species. Species rows with acceptedNameUsageID and status synonym, ambiguous synonym, or misapplied are retained as resolving name usages. Provisionally accepted names are reported but excluded from the accepted baseline.
limitations: Catalogue of Life reports this Base Release as about 80% complete; it is a versioned authoritative checklist baseline, not a claim that all living species have been discovered or described.
Nomenclatural coverage is independent of Evo Atlas dossier, evidence, media, fossil, ecology, translation, and expert-review maturity.
Two accepted species rows have no source checklist datasetID in the upstream archive; their stable Catalogue of Life IDs are retained and the missing lineage is reported.
Changes in later Catalogue of Life releases require an explicit new snapshot and concept-level diff; this immutable release is never silently rewritten.

Catalogue of Life usage IDs are authoritative locators within this snapshot but are not guaranteed to remain unchanged across sector resynchronizations; future release diffs must also compare source checklist and name-concept fields.

search.normalization: Unicode NFKD; remove combining marks; lowercase en-US; replace non a-z0-9 runs with spaces; trim

acceptedTargets.routing: SHA-256 of the exact release-scoped usage ID; first two lowercase hexadecimal characters
acceptedTargets.relationshipToAcceptedSpeciesCount: These minimal target records make every resolving name locally dereferenceable. They include non-species ranks when referenced and never increase counts.acceptedSpecies.

hierarchy.scope: Every accepted species plus the ancestor closure of every accepted species parent, with higher taxa restricted to accepted and provisionally accepted non-species usages and direct-child edges for every node with a parent.
hierarchy.routing: SHA-256 of the exact release-scoped node ID or parent ID; first two lowercase hexadecimal characters select a shared route. Route files are Windows-safe and checksum-declared; no per-parent files are emitted.

nodeRecordSchema.id: Catalogue of Life usage ID for an accepted species or higher-taxon closure node
nodeRecordSchema.parentId: Parent higher-taxon usage ID, or null for a root
nodeRecordSchema.sourceDatasetId: ChecklistBank source-sector dataset ID or null when absent upstream
nodeRecordSchema.childCount: Number of locally projected direct children, including accepted species and closure nodes

childRecordSchema.parentId: Higher-taxon parent usage ID used for routing and filtering
childRecordSchema.sourceDatasetId: ChecklistBank source-sector dataset ID or null when absent upstream
childRecordSchema.childCount: Number of locally projected direct children; zero for accepted species

relationshipToAtlas: This registry covers names and taxonomic placement only. It does not imply an Evo Atlas dossier, evidence maturity, media, fossil, ecology, translation, or expert review.
taxonIdScope: Catalogue of Life usage IDs identify records in COL26.8. They are not treated as sufficient cross-release concept identity because source-sector resynchronizations can replace IDs.

recordSchema.normalizedName: Deterministic search key; not a scientific name
recordSchema.id: Catalogue of Life usage ID in this snapshot
recordSchema.rank: species for every record in this registry
recordSchema.acceptedId: Target accepted usage ID for resolving names; null for accepted species
recordSchema.parentId: Parent usage ID for accepted species; null for resolving names
recordSchema.sourceDatasetId: ChecklistBank source-sector dataset ID or null when absent upstream
recordSchema.classification: Ordered values named by classificationFields; trailing nulls omitted
